11.text: In one tale a young man goes to the dead body of his father for

12.text: protection. But the corpse says, “I cannot keep you near me. I am disin-

13.text: tegrated, and my house is very cold.” After that the “spirit” instructs the

14.text: young man how to win the young daughter of a rich reindeer-breeder. In

15.text: still another very characteristic and widely known tale, a young girl finds in

16.text: the country a bare skull, and takes it home. She conceals it in her clothes-

17.text: bag, and from time to time takes it out and laughs at it. And the bare

18.text: skull returns the laugh. At last her mother takes notice of something unusual

19.text: in her behavior, and finally discovers the skull. The whole family are panic-

20.text: stricken. They flee, leaving the girl alone and without any means of sub-

21.text: sistence. The girl begins to lament before the skull, and, in a paroxysm of

22.text: despair, she even kicks it with her toes. The skull departs in search of its

23.text: body, and soon comes back in the shape of a fine young man, bringing

24.text: along a large herd and a long train of sledges. After that they lived happily.

25.text: This tale represents the corpse as being at the same time something much

28.text: FUNERAL, REINDEER CHUKCHEE. — Immediately after death, the body is

29.text: stripped of all its clothing, including necklace and amulets, and laid in the

30.text: sleeping-room between two skins with the leather side turned inward, so that

31.text: one serves as bedding and the other as covering. It is considered more or

32.text: less sinful to “show to the daylight” the dead body, especially its face and

33.text: genitalia. The inmates of the house must leave the room; but one man at

34.text: least must stay all the time with the body, because, should it be left alone,

35.text: it might revive, and do harm. This, by the way, refutes the previous assertion

36.text: by the natives, that the deceased while in the house is “good.”

37.text: The funeral ceremony is performed on the day after death; and during

38.text: the night there must be two watchers, for fear that, in the darkness, one

39.text: man might be roughly handled by the corpse. As soon as a man is dead,

40.text: and so long as his body is in the house, one of the inmates must act as a

41.text: special enchanter against the evil influence of the deceased. This person is

42.text: called the “fortifier” (tanoˊmñᴀlɪn), meaning that he fortifies the people, and
